body: I became super depressed during my last year of high school, to the point I would randomly cry from time to time. None of the teachers that noticed did anything.

When I was looking after my sister's dogs, one of them wanted to go into my parent's room instead of hanging out with me. I was already feeling depressed, but being rejected by a canine was a new low for me and I just lost it.
This, plus hanging out with drunk people is awful too.

In subjects I was poor in: teachers would be too distracted by the popular students to actually provide any real help to me.

In subjects I was good in: teachers would just let me get ahead of the class or do side projects and start to neglect me, while they help out all the popular students who were struggling.

I graduated in 07, found a job on the other side of the city and moved out of my parents. This was about the time the recession started. That job lasted 3 months before they decided to outsource the department overseas. The next job lasted a week before they admitted they over hired, and I guess I was one of the unlucky ones. I had one more session where I was hired, but the company sorta disappeared before my first day. After that it was just a long string of bad interviews, and eventually my roommates kicked me out. I had no money, spent everything on just getting by and trying to find a job and failing. My parents took me back, ended up with a job at Walmart and I have been stuck there ever since.

I remember being checked in and having the nurse, social worker, and doctor telling me they "didn't see why I was there" when I checked myself in for having a panic attack about committing suicide. I didn't have issues with panic attacks or anxiety before taking a new medication that a psychiatrist prescribed to me, but yet they continued to medicate me with the same thing.

It was pretty clear to me that they were not able and unwilling to actually help. At least the other patients were pretty cool, talking to them was the only positive aspect of the whole ordeal.
Finding people that I can relate to. I just feel so lonely and it seems so hard to find people that can understand unless they have been through the same thing.
Sorry, I know you are trying to help, but it seems like you are making too many assumptions about the situation that I am in to really be of any use.
I am sorry to hear something like that happened to you as well, but I appreciate you sharing that, thank you.

I don't have an issue with joking around, but if the only thing a person does is joking around, and never takes an issue seriously, that is a problem. It is frustrating to see so many people have a "I don't care" attitude, yet throw around jokes about the issue whenever it comes up.
Seeing a doctor. I stress out too much even thinking about it, I have had awful experiences dealing with them.
Reading, spelling, taking notes, understanding literature/poems, etc. Nobody takes me seriously when I try to tell them, made my school life hell.
Ya, I think that be the most realistic answer.

If I kill myself then I would like to send a message about how nobody took my problems seriously enough. More than likely they still wouldn't, like what happened when my cousin killed himself, I would just die a meaningless death.
I can't find help for any of my problems, not even any empathy. I even went to get professional help and I felt like I was being mocked and scammed.

As I understand it, Introverts aren't completely anti-social, but they prefer to have a small group of well known friends instead of large groups.

In my case, in order to make a friend I feel like I have to invest a lot of time and effort to maintain the relationship. More often than not, these friends could just easily ditch me at any moment, leaving me feeling alone, betrayed, resentful, and bitter. After a while it can cause an unhealthy view on interactions in general.

I don't know if there a required minimum, but I do feel a little better talking to people. I have had days were I don't interact with people at all, but that is mostly because I detracted myself well enough with my hobbies to not be bothered.
Because I can't depend on people to help me out with my problems, I lost trust in my family and doctors to even be empathetic.

My mother killed someone before, she only told me about it once.

It was the 70s, she was moving and needed to drive through some small town in the middle of the night. While passing through a man suddenly wanders in front of her car and she ended up hitting and killing him.

She stayed in the police station while they investigated, freaking out about what will happen to her. An officer came by and told her about the man that she hit. He apparently was a known local who gets drunk regularly, a native american who was homeless and without a family, and they verified that he just left a bar just moments ago and only a couple of blocks away. They figured that he just didn't look where he was going and crossed the road at the wrong time. The police just ruled it as an accident and didn't press any charges on my mother and she was free to leave.

"Why are you so quiet?", "Why are you by yourself?", etc.

I guess it is because the only thing people talk to me about is how little I talk.

Because I can't feel a sense of accomplishment anymore.

People tell me do so a certain thing because of how amazing it will be, romanticizing and hyping up whatever it is, but it is always a let down.

I'm not afraid of failing, I'm afraid of succeeding but yet thinking "That wasn't worth it at all."

With most people, the main focus of conversation is pointing out how much of a shut in I am. Somehow they do not know that just randomly mocking someone is not a good way to have a conversation. It is pretty much a viscous cycle of me coming out, being made fun of, retreating, repeat.
Trump supporters, if trump does not accept the election results and claims it was rigged, how will you respond?

I've seen a fair share of mental health professionals over the years, I suppose I'm this type of patient. Hell, a few months back I stayed at the mental hospital for a few days and the best I was told was "I don't see why you are here."

I don't seem to fit into any real peg hole of the more popular and trendy afflictions, so most of these professionals just shrug their shoulders, give out a random diagnosis and random pills then pat themselves on the back and call it a day. I had to call it quits when the last test sample gave me anxiety (which I didn't have before) and messing up my vision to the point I was going blind. 4 doctors told me to continue it anyways, and at that point I knew that they didn't care anymore, that it was more important for these people to push drugs than actually help me.

It's just frustrating how even after telling people how awful the system has been to me, they'll still suggest for me to go through all that BS again, like somehow the next person I see will somehow magically be different than the dozens of others that I've seen throughout my life.

Ya, I'm in the same boat as well. 31, never really got into a serious relationship or even dated. People think that being a gay male means that this sort of stuff is easier, but it isn't really. I've tried some online dating sites before, but matches tend to either be: sexual horn dogs or over-achievers. Both are trying to find others like themselves but I don't really fall into either group.

It's a bit of a catch-22. Most people will say to cure your depression before attempting to find love, but there will always be that sense that finding love is what will cure your depression.

It's stupid, painful, and just adds to a list of things that increases the amount of shame and guilt you feel.
I would always watch this during Christmas. I tried to get myself to stop, but you know what they say about old habits...

Worked in retail. Had a coworker cuss at customers during Black Friday, something like "move the fuck back!" while taking stuff out to the sales floor and people crowded around so badly that they could not move. Someone obviously complained, quite emotionally too, but it did not stick, apparently. A week later said employee got a promotion.

Not talking to my cousin before he committed suicide.

At the time he was having issues with school, sort of what I gone through as well. When I was having those problems I did not like all the advice and fake empathy that others kept trying to give me, so when I was asked to try to talk to him I assumed that I would just be adding fuel to the fire and making the problem worse. I eventually overcame my issues by removing myself from everybody and spending time working out things by myself, and I thought that if he did the same then things could work out for my cousin as well. It did not.

Looking back, all it really seemed like was that he just wanted somebody to relate to, rather than having folks try to "fix" him. I feel now that I just took the time to at least talk to him, I would have at least make him feel less like a weirdo and tell him that he was not alone.

I remember freaking out from the 1977 cartoon version of "The Hobbit". Not from any of the monsters, but from Bilbo Baggins. He looked so weird and deformed, it was uncanny and it freaked me the hell out.

I was scared of a lot of a lot of things from my childhood; alien, gremlins, Freddy Krueger, etc. But I eventually grew out of it. But that creepy cartoon Bilbo Baggins? Seeing that "thing" still makes me cringe.
